reconstruction.objects: For each natural width n, a basis state is a function from Fin n to Fin 2, hence an n-bit labelled word. The ordinal carrier is Fin(2^n). GrayBasis.equiv is an equivalence between ordinal labels and these bit functions, constructed recursively with least-significant coordinate at wire0. It gives the binary-reflected Gray order under that encoding.
reconstruction.recursive_formula: Write a legal (n+1)-bit ordinal i as 2*q+b, with q=i/2 and b=i%2. The new wire0 is b when q is even and flipBit(b) when q is odd; each wire j+1 is equiv(n,q) at j. Thus wire0 is the XOR of the two lowest binary digits of i, and the upper wires apply the same rule recursively. This is a decoded formula, not a separately supplied closed-form XOR theorem.
reconstruction.central_theorem: For any n and first,second in Fin(2^n) with first.val+1=second.val, there exists target in Fin n such that the complete Gray bit function of second equals the complete Gray bit function of first with only target flipped. This is a basis-label equality for strictly successive, non-wrapping ordinal labels.
reconstruction.proof_mechanism: Induction on width separates even and odd first labels. An even first label and its successor share quotient tails, while the low Gray bit flips; target0 suffices. For an odd first label the low Gray bit stays fixed and quotient tails become successive; the inductive target is shifted to target.succ. At width0 no successive pair exists, so the hypothesis is contradictory.
reconstruction.domain_and_order: Natural-number Euclidean quotient/remainder, not signed division. Fin n names physical bit positions. Fin.consEquiv puts its supplied bit at coordinate0 and the recursive word at successors. primitiveBasisLEEquiv flattens b to sum b_j*2^j; it is not a big-endian or reversed-wire encoding.
reconstruction.scope: Three total data definitions and five symbolic arithmetic/basis theorems. No amplitudes, complex scalar assumptions, state norm, phase convention, ancillas, oracle access, measurement, circuit list, matrix conjugation, gate resource ledger or finite-bit complexity is part of these eight signatures. Imported xBasisAction names an X-like basis update but the local theorem does not assemble or evaluate a quantum gate circuit.

providers.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.PrimitiveBasis
providers.definition: abbrev PrimitiveBasis (qubits : Nat) := Fin qubits -> Fin 2
providers.carrier: Exactly one binary value for each named wire; PrimitiveBasis0 has a single empty function.

providers.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.flipBit
providers.definition: flipBit bit := if bit=0 then 1 else 0
providers.meaning: Interchanges the two members of Fin2. Imported flipBit_flipBit certifies involution.

providers.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.xBasisAction
providers.meaning: Changes the target coordinate and leaves every other coordinate unchanged. Its local result type is a bit function, not a quantum matrix.

providers.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.primitiveBasisLEEquiv
providers.definition: PrimitiveBasis q equiv Fin(gridSize q), gridSize q=2^q
providers.meaning: At width0 the unique empty word maps to index0. At successor width, index=bits0+2*index(tail), fixing wire0 as least significant.

providers.name: finProdFinEquiv
providers.definition: Fin m x Fin n equiv Fin(m*n), (a,b) maps to b+n*a; inverse uses divNat/modNat
providers.use: With n=2, ordinal i decomposes into (i/2,i%2), in this order.

providers.name: Fin.consEquiv
providers.use: Constructs the new low wire from the bit after prodComm; upper wires are the recursively generated Gray word.

providers.name: finCongr, Equiv.prodCongr, Equiv.prodComm, Equiv.trans
providers.meaning: Finite bound cast by 2^(n+1)=2^n*2, product equivalence transport, product swap and composition. They change carrier coordinates explicitly rather than postulating an arbitrary permutation.

declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.twist
declarations.signature: def twist (n : ℕ) : Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 ^ n) × Fin 2)
binders: n : Nat, explicit dimension data; no logical hypothesis or hidden typeclass
declarations.meaning: The involutive permutation (q,b) -> (q,b) for q even, and (q,flipBit b) for q odd. Tail q is preserved. Forward and inverse maps are the same; bundled left/right inverse proofs are part of the equivalence, not premises.

declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.equiv
declarations.signature: def equiv : (n : ℕ) → Fin (2 ^ n) ≃ PrimitiveBasis n
binders: n : Nat, explicit dimension data; no logical hypothesis or hidden typeclass
declarations.meaning: A total recursively defined equivalence, not a chosen existential bijection. Width0 uses the inverse empty-word LE encoding. At width n+1 it decomposes ordinal into quotient and remainder, twists the remainder by quotient parity, recursively Gray-encodes the quotient and conses the twisted low bit.

declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.headBit
binders: index : Nat, explicit value; no upper-bound or other hypothesis
declarations.meaning: Return index%2 when (index/2)%2=0, otherwise flip that bit. It is defined on all naturals; no off-domain default or source-dependent oracle is involved.

declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.equiv_head
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem equiv_head (n : ℕ) (index : Fin (2 ^ (n + 1))) : equiv (n + 1) index 0 = headBit index.val
binders: index : Fin(2^(n+1)), explicit finite label whose bound is carried in the type
declarations.meaning: The low coordinate of the Gray equivalence is literally the headBit supplier. No parity assumption is needed; both parity branches are part of the definition. Proof is rfl.

declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.equiv_tail
declarations.signature:
@[simp] theorem equiv_tail (n : ℕ) (index : Fin (2 ^ (n + 1))) (wire : Fin n) : equiv (n + 1) index wire.succ = equiv n ⟨index.val / 2, by
        have bound : index.val < 2 ^ n * 2 := by simpa only [pow_succ] using index.isLt
        omega⟩ wire
binders: wire : Fin n, explicit legal recursive upper-wire coordinate
declarations.meaning: Each upper Gray coordinate is the lower-width Gray code of the quotient index. Quotient legality is derived from index.isLt and the power identity, not assumed separately. Proof is rfl; the displayed Fin-bound proof is proof-irrelevant type-formation data.

declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.headBit_even
declarations.signature: theorem headBit_even (index : ℕ) (even : index % 2 = 0) : headBit (index + 1) = flipBit (headBit index)
binders: even : index%2=0, the sole explicit arithmetic hypothesis
declarations.meaning: At even ordinal steps, the quotient remains fixed, the binary low digit becomes1, and the resulting Gray head flips. No finite-width bound is required.

declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.headBit_odd
declarations.signature: theorem headBit_odd (index : ℕ) (odd : index % 2 = 1) : headBit (index + 1) = headBit index
binders: odd : index%2=1, the sole explicit arithmetic hypothesis
declarations.meaning: At odd ordinal steps, quotient increments and low digit resets to0. The toggled quotient parity compensates for that reset, leaving the Gray head unchanged. No finite-width bound is required.

declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.GrayBasis.adjacent
declarations.signature: theorem adjacent {n : ℕ} (first second : Fin (2 ^ n)) (next : first.val + 1 = second.val) : ∃ target : Fin n, equiv n second = xBasisAction target (equiv n first)
binders: n : Nat, IMPLICIT universally quantified dimension
next : first.val+1=second.val, the sole explicit logical hypothesis
declarations.meaning: Strictly consecutive labels have Gray words related by flipping one legal wire. The statement supplies an existential target, not a named extraction algorithm, a unique-existence declaration, gate list or costed implementation.

signature_notation: Each signature retains namespace-relative Lean source type and binder syntax, with formatting-only line joining except the embedded Fin-bound proof in equiv_tail. The actual compiler #check transcript was separately inspected for all eight, including @adjacent's implicit n. No additional binders were omitted.

boundary_audit.width0: Fin(2^0)=Fin1 has only ordinal0 and PrimitiveBasis0 is the empty bit function. equiv0 is the unique equivalence. adjacent at n=0 is vacuous because 0+1=0 cannot hold; it does not construct a Fin0 wire.
boundary_audit.width1: Gray labels0,1 are bits0,1 and adjacency flips the only wire.
boundary_audit.last_index: The adjacency premise requires second still in Fin(2^n), so first cannot be the maximum label. Last-to-first cyclic adjacency is not supplied.
boundary_audit.arithmetic_cases: headBit accepts every natural; even and odd hypotheses partition parity. For a successor-width equivalence tail quotient is always in Fin(2^n).
boundary_audit.phase_register_resource: No quantum phase, amplitude, clean ancillary register or resource assumption exists in the signatures. They cannot support conclusions about such objects without additional downstream bridges.

checks.finite_diagnostic: A fresh #eval after the pasted module computed LE-flat Gray labels at width3: [0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4]. This is a diagnostic, not the arbitrary-width theorem or a native_decide proof.

discrepancies_or_questions: The module's 'physical X action' phrasing is faithfully decoded as xBasisAction on labelled bit functions. It does not itself prove a compiled quantum gate or matrix action.

The quantified adjacency contract is non-wrapping and existential. A source requiring cyclic closure, a named target algorithm, uniqueness theorem or resource bound would need separate evidence; the withheld source was not inspected.
